title: Point it at a drive or folder
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

This slice creates the scanner, but it is labelled risk tier low. The project's process constraint says scanner slices are cut at a higher tier and that the lightest process cannot tell which ones those are. Should the engine re-tier SL-020 so the counting rules get the harder review?

Is it acceptable for the build to run Microsoft's dotnet-install.ps1 into a gitignored .dotnet/ when no 10.0 SDK is present? If not, someone with admin installs a 10.0 SDK machine-wide once, and eng/dotnet.ps1 becomes a check with no install.
Code-behind only in the window versus a view-model. This is fine for one window, but the next slice (the tree) will add screens and may want the opposite.

The optional path argument as a supported CLI contract versus a test-only hook. It is kept as a contract because validate drives a real drive with it, and it also gives 'pick a folder' a scriptable route.
One Core assembly holding Native, Scanning and Store versus splitting the store into its own project. It is one project now, and the internal write API is what keeps the seam.

Ten test classes plus a fixture for the first slice. This is heavier than the lightest process would pick, but the project constraint requires the five counting-rule tests before any scanner slice can pass.

The test-local CreateSymbolicLinkW with SYMBOLIC_LINK_FLAG_ALLOW_UNPRIVILEGED_CREATE. The design names it as the fix only 'if 1314 ever appears'. File and Directory.CreateSymbolicLink worked unelevated in every run (LinkTests and ListingFallbackTests pass), so it was not needed.

The architecture's Scan Engine asks the volume for used space on a whole-drive scan, to show the coverage gap. This slice's design has no component for it. On C: this run found 685.8 GB on disk against about 735 GB used, with 599 unreadable folders. That gap is what the coverage panel would show.

A bare `dotnet` in this repo now fails, deliberately: global.json pins 10.0.100 and the machine has only 9.0.318. Every build, test and publish must go through eng/dotnet.ps1. Each fresh worktree downloads about 300 MB into its own .dotnet/ unless someone installs a 10.0 SDK machine-wide once (Q-003's stated escape).

Cases C-010 and C-011 are fed by class-level filters (RootTests.: 7 tests; CancellationTests.: 2 tests) because each case bundles several distinct shapes. If the engine needs exactly one method per case, those two classes could become single tests.

U-001 measured WPF's share at about 160 MB, and the 800 MiB store budget in ScanStoreBudgetTests is derived from that. When the tree slice adds the virtualized view, re-measure the whole app at 5M entries against 1 GiB.
The unreadable-folder list builds every path when a scan ends (599 on C:). Fine at this size. The later unreadable panel may want to build paths lazily.
SL-020 is still stored with risk_tier 'low' in the engine DB (slices row 36), although Q-002 decided to raise it to medium. Re-tiering is the engine's step, not this build's.
